leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 ruling on pride parade bans
leads.documents: Documents systemic refusal by Russian cities including Moscow to authorize pride parades as discrimination against gay community; establishes enforcement pattern for public assembly.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades.' No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Russian federal law on 'propaganda' of non-traditional sexual relationships (2013, expanded 2022)
leads.documents: Documents criminalization of distribution of materials promoting non-traditional relationships and materials making minors interested in gender transition; expanded in 2022 to apply to anyone regardless of age.
leads.detail: Cited as 2013 law criminalising distribution of 'propaganda' among minors, expanded in 2022. No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Russian federal law banning gender-affirming care and legal gender changes - July 2023
leads.documents: Documents outright ban on gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition; directly determines trans legal status and access to care.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia - November 2023 extremism ruling and 22 March 2024 unified list entry
leads.documents: Documents designation of 'the international LGBT public movement' / 'international LGBT social movement and its structural units' as extremist/terrorist, criminalizing participation, funding, and display of symbols like rainbow flag.
leads.detail: Cited as November 2023 Supreme Court ruling following Ministry of Justice lawsuit, formally added 22 March 2024 to 'unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons'. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Documents ECHR finding that failure to offer any legal recognition to same-sex relationships violates human rights; notes Russia left court in 2022.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled...' No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Documents condemnation of wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya by five expert advisors.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Documents confirmation that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya took place and was ignored by authorities.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims...' No URL visible.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow rankings - 2016, 2019, 2024
leads.documents: Documents institutional assessment of LGBTQ rights status: Russia second least friendly in 2016, 46th of 49 in May 2019, worst of 49 surveyed in 2024.
leads.detail: Cited as ILGA-Europe ratings. No URL visible in excerpt.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch and International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association - 2007 note
leads.documents: Documents attack on civil rights of LGBTQ people in Russia, shrinking space for discussion, media censorship, and persecution.
leads.detail: Cited as: 'In 2007, Human Rights Watch and the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association noted...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Amnesty International - statement on Supreme Court extremism ruling / Reuters on EU sanctions March 2021
leads.documents: Documents human-rights characterization of extremism ruling as 'shameful and absurd' and criminalization effect; Reuters documents EU economic sanctions on two Chechen officials accused of persecuting LGBTQ people.
leads.detail: Cited as Amnesty International described ruling as 'shameful and absurd'; Reuters reported March 2021 EU sanctions. No URLs visible.
